strings.name: Bola Tinubu
strings.summary: US-trained accountant Tinubu moved from business to the Senate and Lagos governorship, later helping establish the APC. President since 2023, he removed fuel subsidies and changed foreign-exchange policy, amid cost-of-living pressure and political debate. His career links urban finance, national coalitions and security; he continued public policy appearances in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His Lagos and presidential leadership affects fiscal, energy and regional policy in Africa’s most populous country.

strings.highlights.h1.text: Worked on finance and urban governance across two gubernatorial terms.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Economic reform
strings.highlights.h2.text: Pursued subsidy and currency reforms, prompting debate over costs and development.

strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed improved security-service welfare and inaugurated skills projects.

strings.timeline.t2.text: Sworn in, announcing an end to fuel subsidies.

strings.timeline.t3.text: Helped unite opposition parties into the All Progressives Congress.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Lagos governor
strings.timeline.t4.text: Took office after democratic-transition elections; re-elected in 2003.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Exile and democracy activism
strings.timeline.t5.text: Worked with opposition abroad under military rule.

strings.timeline.t6.text: Represented Lagos West in the Third Republic Senate.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Returns to Nigerian business
strings.timeline.t7.text: Returned after US employment and joined Mobil Nigeria.

strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed Chicago State studies and began accounting work.
